answer_text: Carbonn has four valencee electrons and a small size, so it forms four strong covalent bonds rather than ions. Catenation lets carbon atoms join in chains and rings, producing a huge family of compounds. A homologous series, such as the alkanes, has the same general formula and functional group; neighbours differ by CH2, chemical reactions stay alike, and boiling points rise with chain length. Alkanes are saturated becuase they contain only C-C single bonds. Alkenes such as propene, C3H6, are unsaturated. They decolourise bromine water and add hydrogen over a nickel catalyst: C3H6 + H2 -> C3H8. This hydrogenation converts vegetable oils into vanaspati ghee. Propanol is the corresponding alcohol obtained by addition of water to propene in the presence of acid.
